#### The checkpoint pair, and what full versus incremental uploads

**What is being answered.** Why a checkpoint is a pair, and what the two checkpointing modes actually upload.

`take(upto)` returns a `Checkpoint(ent, upto)` — the state and the offset in one value. `restore(cp, useOffset)` then shows why they must match: the replay loop starts at `useOffset + 1`, so that one expression is the whole correctness of the recovery. Called with 4 it gives 45; called with 0 it gives 68.

`uploadVolume` prices the modes by their arguments: `countEntries(0, c)` grows with every checkpoint, `countEntries(prev + 1, c)` depends only on the gap. 14 against 8.

The animation steps through the code, holding each line long enough to read the STACK (call frames and their locals) and the HEAP (allocated arrays and objects) as they are AT THAT MOMENT. Expand any step to study it on its own.

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch07-checkpoints-memory/ch07-checkpoints-memory.svg" alt="The checkpoint pair, and what full versus incremental uploads, 4 steps showing stack and heap" width="980">

<details>
<summary><b>Step 1 of 4</b> — the checkpoint writes the state AND the offset</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch07-checkpoints-memory/frames/step-01.svg" alt="Step 1: the checkpoint writes the state AND the offset" width="980">

The Checkpoint carries `ent` and `upto` in one value — 4 entries holding 23, at offset 4. The offset is half the checkpoint, not metadata about it: a snapshot that does not say where it was taken cannot be resumed from.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 2 of 4</b> — restoring with the matching offset gives the no-crash total</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch07-checkpoints-memory/frames/step-02.svg" alt="Step 2: restoring with the matching offset gives the no-crash total" width="980">

The loop starts at `useOffset + 1` = 5, so it adds the 4 events after the checkpoint to the 23 loaded from it: 45, the no-crash total. One expression, `useOffset + 1`, is the entire correctness of the recovery.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 3 of 4</b> — and with a stale offset the prefix is counted twice</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch07-checkpoints-memory/frames/step-03.svg" alt="Step 3: and with a stale offset the prefix is counted twice" width="980">

`restore(cp, 0)` replays from index 1, re-adding events already in `cp.entries`: 68 instead of 45, over by exactly the 23 the checkpoint had already accumulated. Same state, same stream, one wrong argument.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 4 of 4</b> — incremental uploads churn; full uploads everything, every time</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch07-checkpoints-memory/frames/step-04.svg" alt="Step 4: incremental uploads churn; full uploads everything, every time" width="980">

Compare the two accumulators' arguments: `countEntries(0, c)` grows with every checkpoint while `countEntries(prev + 1, c)` depends only on the gap. 14 against 8 here — and the ratio keeps improving, because full tracks total state and incremental tracks churn.

</details>

<sub>Both restore totals and both upload counts are computed from the seed and asserted. Generated by `node tools/gen_ch07.js` on `tools/memkit.js`.</sub>
